messages:
maya: heads-up — keystore-agent started failing decrypts in eu-onprem about 15m ago after we tightened netpols. apps returning 502/timeout. creating thread so sec/infra can triage. :eyes:
incident-bot: INC-2026-03-22-7 created — severity: high, affected: keystore-agent, region: eu-onprem
connor: can you paste the keystore logs (tail) and the node conntrack/sysctl output?
maya: logs snippet:
```
2026-03-22T09:12:01Z [ERROR] decrypt: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: dial tcp 10.10.5.20:443: connect: connection refused
2026-03-22T09:12:01Z [WARN] reconnecting to kms-proxy
2026-03-22T09:12:05Z [ERROR] decrypt: context deadline exceeded
```
and conntrack/sysctl:
```
# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 262144
# conntrack -S | grep "entries"
entries 262144 0 0
# dmesg | tail -n 5
[12345.678901] nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
```
jess: quick question — did someone merge RBAC change to `svcacc-keystore` this morning? I remember a PR touching roles.
samir: yeah i merged a tiny RBAC cleanup (removed unused decrypt list permission) — i did not touch netpols. PR: https://git.internal/r/infra/PR-842
lina: checking audit logs for KMS — the HSM-side audit shows no incoming decrypt calls from the agent IPs during the outage window; only auth token hits. looks like connection never reached KMS.
connor: so hypothesis: conntrack overflow on host + tighter netpol egress means packets dropped, so no TCP handshake to KMS; RBAC change made retry behavior worse (no fallback). need to confirm netpol rules.
maya: here's the netpol that was applied in the change window:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-all-egress
  namespace: keystore
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/8
```
this blocks public KMS endpoints (we rely on proxy 10.10.5.20 though) but if conntrack drops then connection never establishes.
samir: ok i can revert the RBAC cleanup (re-add decrypt role) if that helps, but main thing is restore egress for keystore to kms-proxy IPs and check host conntrack limits.
opsbot: rolling back netpol `deny-all-egress` in keystore namespace (action by ops, id: rb-1712509876)
maya: rollback applied 09:38 UTC — keystore pods restarted, decrypts started succeeding. health checks green. :thumbsup:
connor: can we get a postmortem checklist items now? my suggested action list:
- Add explicit egress allow for kms-proxy IPs in the netpols (avoid broad denys)
- Revert the RBAC cleanup or add a canary warning in the PR template when removing decrypt permissions
- Increase nf_conntrack_max on edge hosts (or tune pod connlimit) and add monitoring alert on `nf_conntrack` table full
- Enhance audit alerts: generate alert when KMS does not receive decrypt calls for >5m while keystore reports errors
- Run a game-day sim for conntrack saturation + netpol tighten to validate fallbacks
jess: I'll open INFRA-571 (netpol: add KMS egress allow + hardening guide) and SEC-389 (RBAC guardrail + PR check). assigning to samir and connor.
samir: assigned, i'll revert my RBAC change as a hotfix and followup with a safety check in PRs.
lina: will add audit rule and a dashboard panel showing decrypt request rate vs agent error rate.
maya: incident resolved and demoted to P2. keeping thread open for postmortem notes. thanks all.
